![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14273146/assets/0d2246fc0a9f60da6796b51f9a410e878130ff5c28ce21d3b4630250263b4aff.png)

The Venn diagram above represents a universal set $S,$ two sets $A$ and $B,$ and the number of elements in each region of $S.$ An element from ${A}^{′}$ is selected at random. Calculate $P({B}^{′}|{A}^{′}).$
question.worked_solution:
To compute $P({B}^{′}|{A}^{′}),$ we need to ask, "what is the probability of $B$ *not* occurring given that $A$ has *not* occurred?"

Since we are assuming that $A$ has *not* occurred, we only consider the elements outside $A.$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14273146/assets/efc4ff11963efa6fee6160f0b14eb4183a3ad3b1ebbecdf6e7f1c0dca1634af6.png)

In total, the number of elements in the event ${A}^{′}$ is

$$
15+5=20.
$$

Of these $20$ elements, $5$ lie outside $B.$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14273146/assets/c4d2d62cf5c2dd51b3a09bc245e73d584340a39542b3933a60fa1b2c91513bb2.png)

Since each outcome is equally likely, $P({B}^{′}|{A}^{′})$ can be interpreted as the proportion of ${B}^{′}$ that lies inside ${A}^{′},$ relative to the size of ${A}^{′}.$ Therefore, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}P({B}^{′}|{A}^{′}) & =\frac{5}{20}=\frac{1}{4}.\end{aligned}
$$
